working_tree: Measured at b1c659e8 plus other agents' uncommitted work of 2026-10-25 — notably CF-21's edits to budgetVsActual's spent side (expenses read on their local day, a per-category list) and essentials.ts (localDay); neither touches a planned figure. Nothing changed but these two files.
mapping: surplus / allocated_this_month → allocatableThisMonth(surplus, allocatedThisMonth) (GoalsScreen.tsx:62 calls it).
nonmonthly_rows {kind, amount} → op.spendCats [{ bucket:'nonmonthly', unit: 'pct' | 'dollar', amount }]; percent_basis → allPct, shown_percent → pct (GoalsScreen.tsx:46).

categories {monthly, need} → op.spendCats [{ bucket:'fixed' (needs) | 'flexible' (flexible), tier: 'critical' | 'important' | 'flex', amount }]; typed_monthly / planned_monthly_average → op.monthlySpending (the one number onboarding writes, modules.tsx 'monthlySpending'); a dated annual bill → a 'nonmonthly' category with months [bill_month]; "no categories" → no spendCats at all.

emergencyTest cash / shock / essentials → emergencyTest(null, cash, shock, essentials); cash_after → cashAfter, months_after → runwayAfter, months_before → jobLossRunway, covers → coversIt, recommended → recommendedFund, gap → gapToFund. Its one production caller is MK-NW-O-004 theEmergencyFund (emergency-fund.ts:242).

savingsByMonth take_home[12] / expenses[12] and annualCashflow gross / tax / employee_k / planned_expenses: the two functions' OWN SOURCE TEXT (src/domain/budget/index.ts) is compiled with their two producers handed in under their own names — incomeMonthlyGrid(op, kind) returning the twelve given months, spendByMonth(op) the twelve given expenses — because the reviewer gives the producers' outputs as the inputs. annualCashflow's year is twelve equal income rows and an expense year with a tenth of it as a December bill (its note: "an annual expense in December to test roll-up"). gross → grossYr, after_tax → netYr, take_home → availableYr, expenses → spendYr, tax → taxYr, k → k401Yr, saved → saveYr.

budgetFromOnboarding monthly_spending / fixed / flexible / annual_bill → op.monthlySpending, a 'fixed' and a 'flexible' category, a 'nonmonthly' bill with months [bill_month] (the categories onboarding's SpendingEditor writes; the legacy b_fixed / b_flexible fields have no writer left and are probed separately below); recurring_base → doc.fixed + doc.flexible (the stored every-month parts), annual_average → doc.monthly_spending, annual_total → doc.monthly_spending × 12 (no reader re-reads a stored doc: saveBudget and loadBudget have no callers — the doc goes straight from buildSnapshot into buildBudgetState, snapshot.ts:143).

budgetVsActual requested_month / recurring_plan / annual_bill / bill_month / actual_non_debt → now = the 15th of that month in 2026; op.spendCats [a 'fixed' category of recurring_plan, a 'nonmonthly' bill with months [bill_month]]; one logged 'Groceries' expense of actual_non_debt on the 10th; planned → planned_total, spent → spent_total, remaining → remaining. Production: BudgetScreen.tsx (`const bva = budgetVsActual(…)`; its planned side is printed in the "Expenses by bucket" header `fig('MK-CF-M-015', … ba.planned)` of the budget editor the Cash flow tab opens — CashFlowScreen.tsx BudgetEditor), HomeScreen.tsx and CashFlowScreen.tsx (spent_total only).

publishSurplus supplied_result → its projectedToSave argument; the answer is the payload it emits on the app's event bus (SURPLUS_CALCULATED), read with the bus's own on(). No production code calls publishSurplus.

ym local_timestamp → the person's device is IN that offset: ym's own source text (essentials.ts) is run in a child node process whose TZ is that zone, on new Date(local_timestamp). (Jest's sandbox cannot change its own zone.)

logged_month_totals {YYYY-MM: amount} → one logged expense per month on the 15th; typed_fallback → essentialsMonthly's typed argument (null → 0, the number its caller hands in when nothing is typed); as_of → now = 2026-10-24 12:00 local.

formula_checks.name: monthlyEssentials
formula_checks.reviewer_why: The algorithm intentionally estimates essentials from recurring categories, but no-category fallback includes all planned spending and ignores the needs distinction. Debts and continuing rent require the higher-level emergency-fund contract.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Label fallback as planned spend, preserve known zero essentials, and ensure debts/rent are added once at the emergency-fund door.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: With no categories it returns the whole planned monthly spend; with categories it adds needs (non-flexible, non-monthly) plus the typed total's remainder over what the plan puts in every month (dated bills excluded). A confirmed all-flexible plan gives $0 (kept). Debts are added once, at the emergency-fund door (minimums), and rent is taken off there once.
formula_checks.plain_example: Typed $2,000, no categories: must-pay $2,000, shown "$2,000/month — you entered"; with a $250 car loan the door reads $2,250.
formula_checks.production_callers: MK-CF-F-010 emergencyTest (fallback); MK-NW-O-004 theEmergencyFund (typed fallback to essentialsMonthly) — Net worth, Job safety, Stress test, Insights
formula_checks.note: App right by his DEC-0251 (the typed plan is the fallback). Records: the card could name DEC-0251 as the reason the no-category figure is the whole plan, and say debts and rent are added at MK-NW-O-004, not here.

formula_checks.name: emergencyTest
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Returns 0 months when essentials is zero and replaces a supplied zero essentials with another estimate. Neither is a valid cash ÷ zero result.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Preserve a confirmed zero denominator; show no finite burn rate/not applicable, or refuse if essentials is unknown.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Essentials of $0 give runwayAfter 0 and jobLossRunway 0; a handed-in $0 is replaced by monthlyEssentials(profile). Its one caller, theEmergencyFund.afterAShock, reads only cashAfter and coversIt and computes its own months (null at $0). StressTestScreen then writes that null as 0 (`runwayAfter: hit.monthsAfter ?? 0`) and prints "about 0.0 months of essentials" (MK-MN-M-025).
formula_checks.plain_example: Cash $6,000, a $1,000 hit, $0 essentials: today "You'd have $5,000 left — about 0.0 months of essentials ($0/month — )"; right: no months figure — $0 essentials, so the cash is not being drawn down.
formula_checks.note: The written formula says "Both are 0 when essentials are 0" — the rule text is wrong too. Smallest change: return null months when essentials ≤ 0 and keep a handed-in 0; and the screen must not turn a null months into 0.0.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-BUDGET): a handed-in $0 is kept; with $0 of essentials no months and no target (null) — the same answer as its door MK-NW-O-004; the Stress test says "there is no count of months to state" and "No target yet".

formula_checks.name: budgetFromOnboarding
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Storing an annual-average expense total alongside the same dated categories risks adding the annual bill again on reread. The persisted field meanings are not established.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Store recurring monthly base separately from annual-average display; retain category timing and prove a round trip.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Stores monthly_spending = plannedMonthlySpend (the year ÷ 12, the bill counted once) and fixed / non_monthly / flexible from spendBuckets. Nothing re-reads a stored budget: saveBudget and loadBudget have no callers; the doc goes straight from buildSnapshot into buildBudgetState, which reads monthly_spending once. So the annual bill is never added twice. Two real defects the reviewer did not reach: (1) no plan at all is stored as $0 (case C02, tenet 3); (2) in the typed-split form (b_fixed / b_flexible, his DEC-7951 household) spendBuckets drops the split once any category exists, so the stored parts $0 + $100 + $0 do not add up to the stored $2,100 (tenet 2).
formula_checks.plain_example: DEC-7951 household ($2,000 typed: $1,100 / $900, $1,200 December bill): stored total $2,100, parts $0 / $100 / $0 — should be $1,100 / $100 / $900.
formula_checks.production_callers: MK-XS-F-031 buildSnapshot (HomeScreen) — its budget feeds only goal capacity and the retirement spend fallback inside the snapshot; no screen prints either
formula_checks.note: APP WRONG on what is stored (parts that do not add up; no plan stored as $0), both latent — no screen reads the stored budget. The double count the reviewer feared is NOT REAL (no reader). Records: the card should say the doc is never saved or re-read.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-BUDGET): the stored parts are each group's year ÷ 12 from spendByMonthByBucket, so they add up to the stored total (DEC-7951 household 1,100 + 100 + 900 = 2,100); the average is stored once ($25,200 a year), nothing reads it back into the typed total, so a dated bill is never added twice; no plan entered stores no plan.

formula_checks.name: budgetVsActual
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Uses average spendBuckets as the selected month’s budget, which understates dated bill months and overstates other months.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Use spendByMonthByBucket for the requested month, the same producer used by This month and Expenses.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: planned = spendBuckets(op): the monthly average, the same in every month, and it leaves out the typed total entirely (only categories, or the legacy typed fields when there are none). This month and the Expenses tab read the dated plan (spendByMonthByBucket) for the same month.
formula_checks.plain_example: Handoff example ($2,000 recurring + $1,200 December insurance): September plans $2,100 (right $2,000), December $2,100 (right $3,200). DEC-7951 household: $100 in every month (right $2,000 / $3,200). Typed $2,000 and no categories: $0 planned, a $500 grocery spend shown red against $0.
formula_checks.production_callers: BudgetScreen (budget editor, opened from the Cash flow tab's budget row / "Set your budget") prints each bucket's "spent / planned" from it; HomeScreen and CashFlowScreen read only spent_total
formula_checks.note: Live. Smallest change: planned (total and per bucket) = spendByMonthByBucket(op)[month of now], the producer This month and the Expenses tab already use. Note: another agent (CF-21) has uncommitted edits in budgetVsActual's spent side today.
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-BUDGET): the selected month's plan from spendByMonthByBucket — the handoff's $2,000 a month + $1,200 December insurance plans $2,000 in September and $3,200 in December ($25,200 a year; $2,100 is only the average).

priority_findings.finding: storing an annual-average total beside dated categories could add the annual bill twice on reread
priority_findings.evidence: No reader re-reads a stored budget: saveBudget and loadBudget have no callers anywhere; budgetFromOnboarding's doc goes straight from buildSnapshot (snapshot.ts) into buildBudgetState, which reads doc.monthly_spending once (the only `doc.monthly_spending` in the file) as the monthly average ($2,883.77 = 34,605.23 ÷ 12 in C03; $2,100 in the handoff example). The bill is counted once. Separate real-but-latent defects: no plan stored as $0; typed-split parts not adding to the total.
